newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to focus on supply, ignore strike.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to focus on supply, ignore strike.

text.p: Linear bonds (OLOs) will focus on new supply on Monday rather than worry about strikes that could cripple the country's railways and some public services, dealers said on Friday.
"We're Belgian. We're used to (strikes). A few people might be in a bit later than normal, but that's about it," one trader said. "We're more interested in what goes on in Bunds."
Railway workers said on Friday they would strike for 24 hours from 10 p.m. on Sunday night, joining a separate strike on Monday by one of Belgium's main public sector union.
Early on Friday the prospect of the Treasury's monthly OLO auction weighed on OLOs 25 and 26, the two lines to be offered, dealers said.

One said, however, the move was in line with early weakness across the curve and was reversed later in the session when comments from various Bundesbank officials calmed fears the interest rate easing cycle in Germany might be over.

Bundesbank Chief Economist Otmar Issing said at a conference in Brussels that his assertion earlier this week that further rate cuts at the moment were not necessary did not mean that they had been ruled out forever.
At a separate conference in Frankfurt, Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said a medium-term cut in Germany's repo rate could not yet be ruled out.
"Issing and Welteke's waltzing around helped," one OLO trader said, referring to Friday's recovery in yields on shorter maturities.
Two-year OLOs ended with yields around 3.47 percent, down from 3.53 in early trade. Five-year issues yielded around 4.80 percent, down from 4.88 at the start of the day.
But OLOs lagged Bunds' rise, with the spread over 10-year German issues widening to 11 from eight basis points.
"It was normal the spread came out a bit," one trader said. "We will stay at these levels ahead of the auction but (the widening) may be a trend."
